name: Winston Churchill
summary: British politician and writer best known for leading a wartime coalition in 1940–1945, sustaining public resistance to Nazi Germany and interpreting events through speeches and historical writing.
zhSummary: 英国政治家与作家，以在 1940—1945 年领导战时联合政府、鼓舞公众抵抗纳粹德国，以及通过演说和历史写作阐述时代事件而闻名。
sections: A political career shaped by experience
在历练中形成的政治生涯

Winston Leonard Spencer Churchill was born on 30 November 1874. Army service, journalism and writing preceded his long parliamentary career, which began with election in 1900. He held several cabinet posts and changed parties during his career. His experience was not an unbroken sequence of successes: the failed Dardanelles campaign in the First World War damaged his standing. This account focuses on his wartime leadership and writing rather than attempting a complete political biography.
温斯顿·伦纳德·斯宾塞·丘吉尔于 1874 年 11 月 30 日出生。他先从事军旅、新闻报道与写作，1900 年当选议员，开始漫长的议会生涯。他曾担任多个内阁职务，也曾改变党派归属。这并非一路成功的经历：第一次世界大战中失败的达达尼尔海峡战役损害了他的政治声望。本文主要介绍其战时领导与写作，而非尝试提供完整的政治传记。
Coalition leadership in 1940
1940 年的联合政府领导

On 10 May 1940 Churchill became prime minister after Neville Chamberlain's resignation. He led a coalition bringing together different political parties at a moment of military crisis. Following the evacuation from Dunkirk and the fall of France, his government continued the war against Nazi Germany. His role included setting strategic priorities, maintaining parliamentary support and working with military commanders; Britain's survival depended also on service personnel, civilians, industry and support from the Empire and Commonwealth.
1940 年 5 月 10 日，内维尔·张伯伦辞职后，丘吉尔出任首相，在军事危机中领导跨党派联合政府。敦刻尔克撤退与法国沦陷后，其政府继续对纳粹德国作战。他的职责包括制定战略重点、维持议会支持及与军事指挥官协作；英国得以坚持抵抗，也依靠军人、平民、工业体系，以及帝国与英联邦各地的支持。
Public expression and an international alliance
公共表达与国际联盟

Churchill's carefully prepared speeches gave language to the dangers and demands of war. Addresses to Parliament in June 1940 combined acknowledgement of danger with a call for persistence. Their importance lay in political communication and morale, not in replacing military action. He also worked to secure American assistance and, after Germany attacked the Soviet Union in 1941, cooperated with Stalin despite deep ideological differences. The Allied victory was a shared military and industrial achievement, not the result of one leader's speeches.
丘吉尔精心准备的演说，为公众理解战争的危险与要求提供了表达。1940 年 6 月的议会演说既承认险境，也呼吁坚持。它们的重要性在于政治沟通与士气，而不能替代军事行动。他还争取美国援助；1941 年德国进攻苏联后，尽管意识形态分歧深刻，他仍与斯大林合作。盟军胜利是共同的军事与工业成果，不能归结为一位领袖的演讲。
The limits of a wartime achievement
理解战时成就所需的背景

Leadership against Nazi Germany must be distinguished from an endorsement of all Churchill's imperial policies. He defended the British Empire and opposed Indian independence for much of his career. The Bengal famine of 1943 unfolded amid wartime disruption, failures of administration and severe shortcomings in relief; the priorities of the British government form part of the history of that catastrophe. These circumstances are necessary context for his leadership, even in an account centred on his contribution to defeating Nazism.
领导抵抗纳粹德国，并不等于其所有帝国政策都值得肯定。丘吉尔维护大英帝国，在政治生涯的很长时期内反对印度独立。1943 年孟加拉饥荒发生于战争冲击、行政失误和救济严重不足的背景下，英国政府的资源分配重点也是这场灾难历史的一部分。即使着重介绍他对击败纳粹主义的贡献，也需要保留这些背景来理解其领导。
Writing history and returning to office
历史写作与再次执政

After defeat in the 1945 general election, Churchill remained prominent in public life. His postwar writing included the six-volume The Second World War, combining historical narrative with his own account of decisions. Such work is valuable testimony but also a participant's interpretation, to be read alongside other records. He received the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1953 for historical and biographical writing and oratory; this was a literature award, not a peace prize.

He served again as prime minister from 1951 to 1955 and died on 24 January 1965. His lasting influence comes partly from the way political action and prose reinforced one another. Evaluating that influence requires separating the effectiveness of his public language, the collective effort of wartime society and the consequences of particular policies.
1945 年大选失利后，丘吉尔继续活跃于公共生活。他战后的著作包括 6 卷本《第二次世界大战回忆录》，把历史叙述与自己对决策的解释结合起来。这些文字具有重要的见证价值，但也是当事人的解读，应与其他记录参照阅读。1953 年，他因历史与传记写作及演说成就获得诺贝尔文学奖；这是文学奖，而非和平奖。
他于 1951 至 1955 年再次担任首相，1965 年 1 月 24 日去世。他的持久影响部分来自政治行动与文字表达的相互促进。评价这种影响，需要区分公共语言的效力、战时社会的集体努力，以及具体政策的后果。

review: 核对1874/1965生卒日、1900议会、1915达达尼尔、1940任首相、1941盟国、1945卸任、1951—1955第二任、1953文学奖。文字不引用未确认录音日期的名句；不把敦刻尔克撤退称胜利，不把军民与盟国贡献归于个人；以IWM史料说明保留孟加拉救济失败背景，不虚构单一原因或死亡数。UK政府及国务院正文已读取；Nobel正文403但索引可读，未绕过；IWM和Bungay相关内容搜索可读。图片采用NARA合作文件197182、PD-USGov，未用Karsh《愤怒的雄狮》。NARA目录原页被工具拒绝，合作导入记录和原始wikitext已保存，不声称重新打开目录。
